steps.title: Determine anesthetic dose and inject urethane
steps.instruction: Weigh the animal, calculate urethane dose (1.4 g per kg body weight), prepare urethane diluted in PBS, and administer the solution intraperitoneally.

steps.title: Maintain temperature during induction
steps.instruction: Place the animal on a heating pad to keep body temperature stable while anesthesia develops.

steps.title: Monitor reflexes for anesthesia depth
steps.instruction: Continuously observe the animal and check ear and paw reflexes to assess the level of anesthesia.

steps.title: Administer first supplemental urethane dose
steps.instruction: After 1 hour, reassess reflexes; if reflexes are still present, give an additional 1/5 of the initial urethane dose intraperitoneally.

steps.title: Administer second supplemental urethane dose
steps.instruction: Continue monitoring; after another hour, if reflexes persist, administer 1/10 of the original urethane dose intraperitoneally.

steps.title: Confirm surgical anesthesia
steps.instruction: Repeat monitoring until surgical anesthesia is reached.

steps.title: Transfer to surgery and monitor temperature
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the animal to the surgical setup, place it on an electric heating pad, and insert a rectal probe to maintain body temperature at 36–37 °C.

steps.title: Fix head in stereotaxic frame
steps.instruction: Secure the head in a stereotaxic frame using ear bars, ensuring stability and proper alignment.

steps.title: Shave cranial hair
steps.instruction: Shave the hair from the cranial area before making the incision.

steps.title: Inject lidocaine for local anesthesia
steps.instruction: Inject approximately 0.3 ml of lidocaine subcutaneously into the shaved scalp using a 30 G needle.

steps.title: Protect eyes with Viscotears
steps.instruction: Apply Viscotears to both eyes to prevent corneal drying and light‑induced damage.

steps.title: Make midline scalp incision
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, make a straight incision along the midline of the skull from anterior to posterior.

steps.title: Clean surgical area
steps.instruction: Remove blood with cotton swabs moistened with PBS and continue cleaning until the area is blood‑free and as dry as possible.

steps.title: Control bleeding with cauterizer
steps.instruction: Use a small vessel cauterizer to stop bleeding in areas with excessive blood; use only in terminal (non‑recovery) experiments.

steps.title: Retract tissue with hemostatic forceps
steps.instruction: Use four hemostatic forceps to hold back tissue, keeping the surgical field open and exposing the maximum skull area.

steps.title: Mark skull coordinates
steps.instruction: Attach a stereotaxic post with its holder and a 22 G needle, then use a fine‑tip marker to mark the ROI coordinates on the exposed skull according to AP and ML positions relative to Bregma.

steps.title: Provide supplemental oxygen
steps.instruction: Place an oxygen mask over the animal’s nose and mouth and deliver oxygen at approximately 0.8 L/min throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Perform craniotomy
steps.instruction: Perform the craniotomy using a manual or electric drill, taking care to avoid damaging the underlying brain tissue, especially near the venous sinus.

steps.title: Keep exposed brain surface moist
steps.instruction: After removing the small piece of skull, place a cotton swab moistened with PBS over the exposed area to keep it continuously wet.

steps.title: Pierce and lift dura mater
steps.instruction: Carefully pierce and lift the dura mater with a 30 G needle that has a slightly bent tip, avoiding damage to the underlying brain tissue to allow electrode insertion.

steps.title: Set up electrode mounting system
steps.instruction: Arrange three stereotaxic posts: one to secure the stimulation electrode and two (each with a pre‑amplifier) to hold Neuronexus recording electrodes; ensure all towers are stable and properly positioned.

steps.title: Insert electrodes and ground
steps.instruction: Place recording and stimulation electrodes in their holders, connect them to the amplifier and stimulator, adjust camera focus, then slowly lower the electrodes respecting AP, ML, and DV coordinates; connect the ground wire to animal tissue, insert the stimulation electrode first followed by recording electrodes, with both stimulator and amplifier turned off.

steps.title: Maintain PBS layer on skull
steps.instruction: Maintain a layer of PBS over the entire skull surface to ensure proper electrical conduction throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Activate recording system and acquire data
steps.instruction: Turn on the Multichannel Systems stimulator and recording amplifier, launch MC_Rack and MC_Stimulus software, and conduct stimulation and recording according to the experimental protocol for the required duration.

steps.title: Remove electrodes and clean
steps.instruction: After recording, carefully remove the electrodes, disassemble the surgical setup, and gently rinse the electrodes with distilled water, avoiding direct water stream contact with the electrode tip.

steps.title: Perform terminal perfusion
steps.instruction: Because urethane anesthesia is toxic and non‑recoverable, subject the animal to terminal perfusion.
